notes: Build order: locomotive (b1-b80), tender (b81-b142), passenger car (b143-b217), tree and signpost (b218-b233). Totals 233 pieces, matching the parts list type by type and colour by colour.

Two separate models, so two groups. The booklet builds the tree-and-signpost scene (b218-b233, pages 63-68) as its own small model. It starts with its own preview box and its own base plate (the white round 4x4, b218). Page 69 shows it standing apart from the train, with no connection between them. I left it unconnected on purpose; linking it to the train would invent a connection the manual does not show.

The locomotive, tender and passenger car are one connected train. They are coupled by ball-and-socket joins (b13 with b92, b87 with b155; pages 42 and 62). The lollipop (b135) and ice-cream cone (b139) are joined to the tender floor plate b81 by their bars. This is an assumption, because the drawings show them lying in the tender bed and do not show exactly how they are held.

Early steps are built upside-down and flipped (pages 7, 29, 45). Some rests_on lists for the wheel arches, base plates, rails and roofs are best estimates from the small drawings. The part types, colours and counts are exact.
The black bracket b67 is added from below to the boiler's lower brick b58 (page 22). I recorded it as an other_join. In the finished loco I treated b67 as resting on the cab's white plate b41.
The two cookie tiles, the lime and orange stacks, the flower and the Santa-hat stack are assumed to sit on the tender's white floor plate b81.
Wheels attach to the wheel-holder plates (lego-4600) by their axle stubs and are recorded as other_joins, not rests_on. Window glass panes are slotted into frames, also recorded as other_joins.
The stacks of round plates (white, red, gold, then a round brick) are listed bottom to top.
